title: Importance of Combat Search and Rescue
description:
Members of the 347th Rescue Group at Moody AFB, Georgia participate in spin-up training before a deployment. This training is meant to increase team cohesion and effectiveness when operating in the deployed environment and hone the combat search and rescue skills necessary for winning today's fight.

1st interview: First Lieutenant (1st Lt) Blair, 38th Rescue Squadron
2nd interview: Captain (Capt) Jesse, 41st Rescue Squadron

transcript.text: - So we really train for anything
and everything could happen.
We have a force on the ground that needs help, whether it's,

in a vehicle, or if somebody fell down a well
or off a cliff and they need technical rescue expertise
to help get one of their guys out, or somebody is hurt,
they're having a bad day,
we hope that those things never happen,

do happen that we're ready to respond.
So this gives us the autonomy
to integrate with really any ground force.
Something that's unique
about the Guardian Angel Weapon System
is we can insert on the ground and link up
with really any ground force, and in any capacity,
to provide technical rescue and integrate that airpower.
- [Soldier] Make sure they don't flank us west, alright?
- It's been great to work with these pilots, you know,
the last couple days I've really figured out
how they operate as a crew.
And for them to work with us, and see how we operate
as a team, and really figure out
what's important to each party.
- [Soldier] Go slow.
- Air Force Combat Search and Rescue
has slowly gotten a name for itself,
because of the great work
that they've done in that joint environment.
There are thousands of people out there, from Navy, Marines,
Army, when things got real bad, and they needed us,
we were there, and we were able to effectively operate,
and rescue a lot of people, and save a lot of lives.
- [Soldier] Get utility here.
- The Department of Defense looks
at Combat Search and Rescue,
or personnel recovery, as a critical mission.
And we're the only unit within the DoD
that that is our sole job.
Our only job is to, day in and day out,
practice personnel recovery, combat search and rescue.
That's something that, every day, we wake up,
and we try to perfect, because,
out there you don't get out 'till you perfect it.
Out there you need to do it.
So we have an opportunity, out here, to train at our peak,
so that we can be out there
and be ready for whatever happens.
